The capital cost for the carbon capture unit is significantly lower than other state-of-the technology due to the higher concentration of CO through water gas shift (leading to a capture volume of 2.8 mtpa from 2 a single train of absorber and regenerator). However, the overall capital cost of the project is comparatively higher due to the following considerations: • The project includes steam and power generation units to minimize dependency on existing operations and the grid. Additionally, an expensive selective catalytic reduction (SCR) unit has been considered both for the boiler and CHP to minimize the project's environmental impact on the combustion of natural gas. Steam and power generation units contribute almost 180 million US$ (i.e., 30%) of the Total Plant Cost. • Capital cost also covers enabling work like relocation and rebuilding of existing facilities, CO 2 pipeline extended to the plant boundary, and natural gas sourcing from the plant boundary.
